name: quaich
author: notation (invented notation / mini-language direction)
description: PRIVATE. An invented stroke notation over the three strokes / - | . There are no visual openers or closers: every stroke can open and every stroke can close, and the closing relation is a 3-cycle -- / is closed by - , - is closed by | , | is closed by / (D = {'/':'-','-':'|','|':'/'}). A word is WELL FORMED if the eager left-to-right reading empties a stack: push the current stroke unless it closes the stroke on top of the stack, in which case pop. It is WHOLE if the stack is empty only after the last stroke (no proper prefix is balanced), i.e. the word is one single nested unit rather than a concatenation of units. Equivalently a whole word is a nesting tree whose nodes are pairs (t, D[t]) and where a node of type t may only carry children of type t or P[t] (P = cyclic predecessor); the eager reading forbids a child starting with D[t]. CLUE: a scrambling of a well formed whole word of 12/14/16/18 strokes (all three strokes present, each at least twice) which is itself NOT well formed. ANSWER: any rearrangement of exactly the same multiset of strokes that is well formed and whole. INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH: (1) the answer is an anagram of the clue; (2) in every valid answer the last stroke is the cyclic successor of the first; (3) so it is a bracket language with an invented non-involutive pairing, read eagerly; (4) top-level concatenation is forbidden (wholeness) -- this is the clause that costs an extra demo, because /-|/ style pair-concatenations look right and score 0. WITNESSES CLOSED: empty string and every constant answer fail the multiset test; the clue itself is guaranteed by generate to be not well formed; sorted order in all three rotations, descending order, reversed clue, palindrome (half+mirror) and greedy pair-concatenation all measured at 0-1% over 500 clues; a uniformly random shuffle scores 0.4%. Only the real rule gets above a few percent. The reference solve builds a RANDOM tree (shape and child order seeded by the clue), never a canonical fully nested chain, so demos do not hand over a template. ITERATION 1 RESULT (lab-quaich-1, 2 Opus players, 6x0.5s rounds + 3s final): MIXED, on target. quaicha CRACKED (final 3539/3539) on round 5-6 using 3 demos; quaichb PARTIAL (final 728/3149 = 23%) and never found the rule, plateauing on a bigram model + best-of-16 sampling. OPEN WITNESS FAMILY (deliberately left open): quaicha did not find the nesting/eager semantics but did recover the pair-count decomposition -- with a=#'-', b=#'|', c=#'/' they compute p=(a+b-c)/2, q=a-p, r=b-p (exactly the a/b/c pair multiset above) and emit a fixed three-block layout '/^r |^r -^p |^p /^q -^q' with case splits for r=0, q=0 and for a first block longer than the last. Verified 600/600 here. It is an earned construction, not a degenerate answer: it requires discovering that each stroke pairs with one specific OTHER stroke, which is the central insight; only the nesting layer is bypassed. Measured attempts to close it are not worth it: a 'no run of k identical strokes' clause removes 54% (k=3) / 14% (k=4) of the accepted set while still leaving the family valid on 20% / 51% of clues, and the player's existing block-splitting logic would re-fit it; a 'some node has >=2 children' clause does not separate either (83% of the family vs 99% of random valid words). Closing it properly needs positional information in the clue (the hole-completion variant, idea 6 in NOTES_notation.md), i.e. a different challenge. Left as is.
